Title: Jyhad:  New player puzzling it out

Messages.Author: David Hewitt
Messages.Body:
OK, well, I played my first full game of Jyhad tonight, and really enjoyed 
it.  I lost, but I liked it.
  We've had some things come up that we weren't able to puzzle out on our 
own...maybe we're just being dense.

First, when, exactly do you tap a minion?  Most cases are obvious, but if you 
play an "augment action" (I think they're called) card, does that tap you?  
Same for if you play a "reacion" card.  We had the same question for voting, 
due to the FAQ, but I see that has been answered.

We are a little unclear as to the difference between augmented action and 
reaction cards, and which can be played on what when.

What, exactly, CAN a tapped vampire do?  Obviously, they can vote.  Can they 
play vote cards, to add more votes?  Is there anything else they can do?

Can two generation 1 vampires work together to rescue a vampire from Torpor?

I'm sure there were more, but its 4 AM so they'll have to wait.

Great game, by the way, if I forgot to mention it.

Ah...which Methusela gets first chance to call for a vote for a blood hunt?  
And can they then play cards relating to "votes you proposed"?

And how are we supposed to determine seating, anyway?

--Dave

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
David Hewitt <khyron@primenet.com> wrote:
>First, when, exactly do you tap a minion?  Most cases are obvious, but if you 
>play an "augment action" (I think they're called) card, does that tap you?  
>Same for if you play a "reacion" card.  We had the same question for voting, 
>due to the FAQ, but I see that has been answered.

Declaring an action taps the acting minion.  Simply using a reaction card
doesn't tap the minion unless the card says so, but successfully blocking
will lead to the blocking minion becoming tapped.  Vampires don't tap
when they vote.  Basically, minions only tap when they act or enter combat.

>What, exactly, CAN a tapped vampire do?  Obviously, they can vote.  Can they 
>play vote cards, to add more votes?  Is there anything else they can do?

About all they can do is vote and use cards that say "usable by a
tapped vampire"  :)  Note that when you burn a political card for a vote,
it is the player burning the card and not a vampire.  Thus it can be done
even if you have no ready vampires.

>Can two generation 1 vampires work together to rescue a vampire from Torpor?

Sadly, no.

>Ah...which Methusela gets first chance to call for a vote for a blood hunt?  
>And can they then play cards relating to "votes you proposed"?

Because you can't use action modifiers or reaction cards during a
bloodhunt vote, I can't think when it would ever matter.  I suppose
that you would count clockwise from the acting player if it might matter.

>And how are we supposed to determine seating, anyway?

Randomly.  I like the house rule that whoever goes first picks
the seating order, though.
